openings.claim: Two removable padded strip jaws at opposite sides could resist lateral slip while distributing compression; feasibility depends on accessible rim geometry.
openings.delta: Change the carrier from a strap alone to two upper/lower aluminum-strip pairs, each bolted outside the hatch and trough. Capture rubber pads between jaws and surfaces without adhesive. Mark jaw placement and tighten alternately rather than loading the left corner alone. Remove both assemblies completely for inspection; keep bolts, nuts and pads together using cord loops and recover them beside the fixture.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, strap-only friction retention, distributed jaws should reduce lateral displacement without reproducing the opposite-corner lift. Success requires position error at most 1 mm after ten openings, resistance to 20 N, reopening within 30 seconds, and no new visible seal tears, including the final right-contact card disturbance. This is an unmeasured prediction; straps could perform equally well.
openings.probe: First use ruler and loose strip placement to determine whether two padded jaws can straddle hatch and rim with every bolt outside existing material and without permanent deformation. If feasible, drill only the strips and fabricate within ninety minutes. Conduct ten opening/closure/pull cycles within twenty observation minutes, with the supplied 1 mm card at the marked right contact on the final closure. Record position, corner lift, reopening time and visible seal condition each cycle; stop on damage or inability to seat. This uses one configuration and ten of twelve allowed trials. It tests outcome feasibility, but does not establish superiority over the untested strap rival.
assumptions: Accessible underside and outboard bolt clearance are indispensable and unprovided.
Four strips and six bolts must accommodate two jaws without additional carriers.
Rubber friction, strip stiffness and seal-safe clamping force are unknown.
Defeat conditions include jaw slip, card-induced rocking, opposite-corner lift, damage, fabrication overrun or reopening over thirty seconds.

assessment: A bounded candidate probe, not deployment. If the geometry check fails, no feasible joint is established from the supplied resources; do not alter the hatch, rim, seal or opening to rescue it.
